h1: Scaling Platform — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference built on white #F2F1F0 and bright teal #15BCDF, set in Quantico and measured against 100vh sections.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — looping video, Quantico, 1s transitions and a masked headline reveal.
about: Scaling Platform is a working reference for an AI or SaaS product: the landing page laid out, measured and ready to rebuild. The palette runs white #F2F1F0 underneath, black #3A3A3A for the type and bright teal #15BCDF carrying the accents, and the type is Quantico. It ships as a single component, so the whole landing page can be lifted into a project without a design handoff. Motion is confined to 1s transitions and a looping video bed. Use it as the reference when you are building an AI or SaaS product landing page and want a finished composition instead of a starting point.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: The row spends its contrast in one place: the #15BCDF action, with the wordmark and the links held back on the ink colour. A mobile overlay takes over below the tablet breakpoint. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #15BCDF action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: Measured, not eyeballed
layout.body: The brief states its sizes at capture (100vh sections, 20px spacing steps and 1s transitions), so a rebuild can be verified instead of approximated. The type and the layout share the same steps, so nothing drifts when one of them is substituted.

layout.title: Weights named per role
layout.body: The size steps and tracking in the brief are what give this its tone: Quantico at a tight display size, then a clear drop to the supporting copy. Substituting the face is possible, but the proportions have to survive the swap. One face, clear roles.

layout.title: A bar with nothing spare
layout.body: The bar sits over the 1916x1080 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

motion.title: Short, named durations
motion.body: Transitions are specified at 1s, which is the timing the controls are held to. Easing is specified alongside the duration (1s), so a rebuild cannot quietly substitute a different feel. Do not ship the browser default.

motion.title: A small interactive surface
motion.body: The interactive layer is deliberately small: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card. Nothing on the page opens a modal or hijacks the scroll; the interactions stay local to the element. Fewer states, fully specified.

fonts.name: Quantico
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

notes: Transitions are specified at 1s, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.

editorial.title: The timing behind the landing page
editorial.body: A preset animation library would give you more movement than this. The brief asks for less: 1s transitions, a 5.1s media loop and a masked line reveal, and nothing decorative on top. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

editorial.title: How Scaling Platform sequences the first read
editorial.body: A strict order costs you flexibility later. Add a section above the fold and 100vh sections and 20px spacing steps have to be re-cut, because the sequence is load-bearing rather than decorative. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What to change first in Scaling Platform
editorial.body: Most people start with the accent colour. Start with the promise instead: rewrite the display line, then re-test bright teal #15BCDF against your own media. Set the new copy at the same display size and re-check the contrast before you add anything.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the Scaling Platform landing page in a different stack?
faq.answer: Scaling Platform was built in a single component, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What can I do with the Scaling Platform brief once I have it?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 5,231-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Scaling Platform actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1916x1080, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

audience: Hand a single component to the engineer with the 1916x1080 crop attached, then let them rebuild it.
Made for a designer joining a project that already ships a single component and only needs the copy replaced.
